intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene (607429) on chromosome 10p12.1.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: Homozygous PDSS1 mutation identified as cause of CoQ10 deficiency in family 1; COQ10D2 designation is nomenclature.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 gene is located on chromosome 10p12.1.
checks.evidence_quote: A genome-wide search for homozygosity in family 1 identified a region of chromosome 10 encompassing the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1)
checks.explanation: Paper places PDSS1 on chromosome 10; band 10p12.1 is standard location nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 is a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) disorder (Mollet et al., 2007). The PDSS1 gene encodes subunit 1 of prenyldiphosphate synthase (Mollet et al., 2007). Nardecchia et al. (2021) stated that PDSS1 acts in the first step of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) synthesis, as part of a heterotetramer, decaprenyl diphosphate synthase, that is involved in synthesizing a side chain of the appropriate length.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 is a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1) and OH-benzoate polyprenyltransferase (COQ2) mutations in ubiquinone deficiency and oxidative phosphorylation disorders.
checks.explanation: The title frames the disorders as OXPHOS disorders.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 gene encodes subunit 1 of prenyldiphosphate synthase.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1), which encodes the human ortholog of the yeast COQ1 gene, a key enzyme of CoQ10 synthesis
checks.explanation: Gene name stated.

checks.claim: PDSS1 acts in the first step of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: PDSS1 and PDSS2 genes encode two proteins (DPS1 and DLP1) implied in the first step of CoQ10 synthesis
checks.explanation: The paper says PDSS1's product acts in the first step of CoQ10 synthesis.

checks.claim: PDSS1 is part of a heterotetramer, decaprenyl diphosphate synthase.
checks.evidence_quote: consist of a heterotetramer, called decaprenyl diphosphate synthase, involved in the synthesis of the appropriate length chain.
checks.explanation: The paper says the PDSS1 and PDSS2 proteins form the heterotetramer decaprenyl diphosphate synthase.

checks.claim: Decaprenyl diphosphate synthase, which includes PDSS1, is involved in synthesizing a CoQ10 side chain of the appropriate length.
checks.evidence_quote: consist of a heterotetramer, called decaprenyl diphosphate synthase, involved in the synthesis of the appropriate length chain.
checks.explanation: The paper says the enzyme makes a chain of the appropriate length. The surrounding text identifies this chain as CoQ10's polyisoprenoid side chain.

paragraphs.text: In patients from a family with CoQ10 deficiency (family 1), Mollet et al. (2007) found that quinone-dependent OXPHOS activities were in the range of the lowest control values. CoQ10 deficiency was confirmed when the addition of quinone restored normal OXPHOS activities.

checks.claim: In patients from family 1 with CoQ10 deficiency, quinone-dependent OXPHOS activities were in the range of the lowest control values.
checks.evidence_quote: In both cases, enzymologic studies showed that quinone-dependent OXPHOS activities were in the range of the lowest control values, while OXPHOS enzyme activities were normal.
checks.explanation: Applies to both families, including family 1.

checks.claim: In patients from family 1, CoQ10 deficiency was confirmed when the addition of quinone restored normal OXPHOS activities.
checks.evidence_quote: CoQ10 deficiency was confirmed by restoration of normal OXPHOS activities after addition of quinone.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous PDSS1 mutation in affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency (family 1). This finding is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: A homozygous PDSS1 mutation was identified in affected members of family 1 with CoQ10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: A genome-wide search for homozygosity in family 1 identified a region of chromosome 10 encompassing the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1), which encodes the human ortholog of the yeast COQ1 gene, a key enzyme of CoQ10 synthesis. Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution
checks.explanation: Homozygous PDSS1 mutation in family 1.

checks.claim: The homozygous PDSS1 mutation in family 1 is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance of COQ10D2.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: The abstract reports homozygosity but never states autosomal recessive inheritance; that is an inference.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency (family 1), Mollet et al. (2007) sequenced the PDSS1 gene and identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution that changes a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E). Mollet et al. (2007) then transformed a yeast Deltacoq1 strain with a mutant yeast COQ1 gene carrying the corresponding mutation. The transformed strain grew poorly on respiratory medium. The human PDSS1 gene itself was not used in this complementation assay.

checks.claim: Affected members of family 1 with CoQ10 deficiency underwent sequencing of the PDSS1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: PDSS1 was sequenced in family 1.

checks.claim: Affected members of family 1 carried a homozygous PDSS1 nucleotide substitution resulting in a D308E change.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 D308E substitution changes a conserved amino acid.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: A yeast Deltacoq1 strain was transformed with a mutant yeast COQ1 gene carrying the mutation corresponding to PDSS1 D308E.
checks.evidence_quote: Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively
checks.explanation: Deltacoq1 was transformed with mutant yeast COQ1, implicitly carrying the corresponding mutation.

checks.claim: The yeast Deltacoq1 strain transformed with mutant COQ1 carrying the D308E-corresponding mutation grew poorly on respiratory medium.
checks.evidence_quote: resulted in defective growth on respiratory medium, indicating that these mutations are indeed the cause of OXPHOS deficiency
checks.explanation: Defective growth on respiratory medium.

checks.claim: The human PDSS1 gene was not used in the yeast complementation assay of the D308E mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively
checks.explanation: The use of yeast COQ1 rather than human PDSS1 is implied by the wording, but the abstract does not explicitly say the human PDSS1 gene was not used.

clinical_synopsis.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain

clinical_synopsis.feature: Coenzyme Q10 deficiency, confirmed by restoration of OXPHOS activities after addition of quinone
clinical_synopsis.hpo_label: Decreased level of coenzyme Q10 in skeletal muscle

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency (family 1), Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous asp308-to-glu (D308E) substitution in the PDSS1 gene, which changes a conserved amino acid. When Mollet et al. (2007) transformed a yeast Deltacoq1 strain with a mutant yeast COQ1 gene carrying the corresponding mutation, the strain grew poorly on respiratory medium.

checks.claim: Affected members of family 1 with CoQ10 deficiency carried a homozygous asp308-to-glu (D308E) substitution in PDSS1.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: D308E = asp308-to-glu.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 D308E substitution changes a conserved amino acid.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: A yeast Deltacoq1 strain transformed with a mutant yeast COQ1 gene carrying the mutation corresponding to PDSS1 D308E grew poorly on respiratory medium.
checks.evidence_quote: Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively, resulted in defective growth on respiratory medium
checks.explanation: Stated directly.
